title: oy says /oy/
parentNote: oy says exactly what oi said yesterday — boy, toy, joy, enjoy. Your child cannot hear any difference between them, because there is none, and the choice is made the same way ay and ai made it: oi goes in the middle, with sounds after it (coin, boil, point), and oy goes on the end, where the word stops (boy, joy, enjoy). Say the rule once and then let the pairs do the work — boil and boy, join and joy are in here side by side on purpose. The slip to expect is not in the reading but in the confidence: a child who reads boy correctly will often still ask whether it ought to be boi, and the honest answer is that they are right to think it sounds the same, and English simply keeps two spellings and parks each one in its own place.

activities.text: The boy did drop the toy in the damp soil, and I did dig it out.
Roy and I do enjoy a trip to the sea, and I want to take the toy boat.
Do they want to join us, or do they want to stay in and sort the toys?

activities.title: Roy and the toy boat
activities.prompt: Read the story one line at a time. Tap any word you want to hear again.
lines: Roy did want to sail the toy boat at the pond.
It is a joy to see it float, but then the wind did get up.
The boat did spin round and round and did land in a reed bed.
Roy did moan. The toy is stuck, and the soil at the rim is damp.
Then I did point at a long stick on the ground.
Roy did grab it and did poke at the reed bed.
Out did pop the boat, and a big frog did pop out with it.
The frog sat on the toy boat and did not want to get off.
Roy did grin and did sail the frog round the pond.
That is a toy boat and a frog. Roy did enjoy that a lot.
